title: How to read the Alignment Taxonomy
introduction: The Alignment Taxonomy examines how evidence from an occurrence relates to a defined governance invariant. Its results are bounded by the actions, conditions and evidence assessed.

parts.title: How to read the Alignment Taxonomy

sections.title: Fidelity Families, Fidelity Classes and invariants
paragraphs: A Fidelity Family groups related governance properties. A Fidelity Class defines a particular property and its governing invariant. An invariant states the condition that should hold within the class boundary. Fidelity names the property examined; it does not presume an Aligned result.

Read a class in this order: governed property and definition, invariant, success and failure conditions, recognition criteria, exclusions, examples and external references. The success and failure conditions describe different evidence tests. They are not automatic opposites.

sections.title: Aligned, Not aligned and Boundary
paragraphs: Aligned requires affirmative evidence that the invariant held under the assessed conditions. The class success condition and all required success-recognition conditions must be satisfied. Not aligned requires the failure condition and all required failure-recognition conditions, subject to the class exclusions.

Boundary identifies a relevant governance relationship for which the evidence does not establish either decisive outcome. The assessment must explain the unresolved condition. An unreviewed observation is not automatically a Boundary result.

Absence of failure evidence does not establish Aligned. Absence of success evidence does not establish Not aligned. Exclusion from failure recognition does not establish Aligned. A failure to satisfy success recognition does not establish Not aligned.
Structured records retain the relationship names successful-invariant, failure-occurrence and ambiguous-boundary. Their public result labels are Aligned, Not aligned and Boundary.

sections.title: Scope, mixed results and exemplars
paragraphs: A result belongs to the assessed action or source clause and its governance boundary. Different actions in one Incident can receive different results. An Aligned result for one boundary does not establish that every action or aspect of the system was Aligned.

Incomplete adjudication remains explicit. Completed clause findings remain available while other material observations await review. A reviewed observation can also have no current Fidelity Class that applies; it must not be forced into a class.

An Aligned finding does not automatically admit an Incident to the exemplar collection. Exemplar admission is a separate governed decision. An admitted exemplar demonstrates the stated invariant within its recorded evidence and boundary conditions.

sections.title: Independent external requirement assessments
paragraphs: An external reference can explain or support a Fidelity Class. A class-to-requirement relationship can identify a requirement for review. Neither relationship determines the result for an occurrence.

VIGIL compares each retained external requirement independently with the occurrence evidence. These assessments use Aligned, Not aligned and Boundary. A taxonomy result must not be copied into an external requirement result.

For an external requirement, Boundary means the requirement is genuinely relevant but a decisive occurrence fact is missing. The assessment basis names that fact. A requirement that is not relevant is excluded from the published assessment rows. An empty assessment table makes no positive alignment or compliance claim.

sections.title: Normative force, relevance and timing
paragraphs: Normative force describes the authority of the external source. It is separate from the alignment result. A voluntary standard or framework can receive any of the three results. A Not aligned result against voluntary guidance does not by itself establish a legal breach.

A binding-law label identifies the source category. It does not establish that a provision was in force or legally applicable to the actor and occurrence. Review must consider the requirement scope, actor, activity, jurisdiction, publication date and any commencement or transition conditions.

A requirement published after the occurrence does not create a retrospective Not aligned result. Where the occurrence date or a decisive scope condition is unknown, the assessment must preserve that uncertainty and explain its significance. VIGIL assessments compare bounded occurrence evidence; they do not establish certification, legal liability or organisation-wide compliance.

sections.title: Separate Harm Impact assessment
paragraphs: Harm Impact assesses materialised consequences under the VIGIL Harm Impact Methodology. Taxonomy classification assesses the governance invariant. External requirement assessment compares the occurrence with a separate requirement. These are distinct questions.

Severity does not determine an alignment result. An occurrence can be Not aligned even where materialised harm is limited or unreported. A harmful consequence does not by itself establish a particular taxonomy or external requirement result.

Each harm dimension is assessed independently. The highest supported assessed severity band controls overall severity; dimensions are not averaged or summed. Unreported harm is not automatically S1. SU records unresolved severity, not a severity band.
The full Harm Impact chapter remains after the Fidelity Family chapters. It provides the dimensions, severity criteria and supporting methodological references.
